author: NorthEast News Desk
body: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover, who commanded and piloted the Artemis II flight around the moon in April, are stepping away from active astronaut duty.

NASA said both will remain connected to the lunar exploration program as emeritus astronauts. In that role, they will volunteer time to train and mentor agency workers and share lessons from the mission with teams preparing for future flights.

Glover has taken a leadership position at California Polytechnic State University, where he is expected to help shape long-term strategy and encourage students in science and engineering. Wiseman’s next plans were not disclosed; his status change is scheduled to take effect during September.

Artemis II carried Wiseman, Glover, NASA astronaut Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen around the moon, setting a new human distance record. Hansen retired from the Canadian Space Agency in July, leaving Koch as the only crew member still on an active astronaut roster. Wiseman previously spent more than five months aboard the International Space Station and served as NASA’s chief astronaut. Glover flew a nearly six-month SpaceX mission to the station before Artemis II. Their new emeritus roles are intended to preserve that operational experience for NASA’s continuing moon program.
dek: Commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover will continue supporting NASA’s lunar program as emeritus astronauts after April’s record-setting moon flight.
headline: Artemis II leaders step away from active astronaut duty
